stem: Which one of the following rulers of Magadha was the contemporary of Alexander, the Great?
expl: The last ruler of the Nanda dynasty was Dhanananda, who was a contemporary of Alexander. Greek writers called him Agrammes. Xenophon describes him as a very wealthy person. Bhaddasala was his commander-in-chief.

stem: Who recognized Sandrokottos as Chandragupta Maurya?
expl: William Jones was the first scholar who identified Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus) with the Mauryan ruler Chandragupta Maurya. Appian and Plutarch described Chandragupta Maurya as Androkottas/Androcottus, while Justin, Strabo, and Arrian mentioned him as Sandrokottas (Sandrocottus). Plutarch and Justin also mention the meeting between Chandragupta Maurya and Alexander the Great.

stem: The first empire was established by which ruler in India?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Chandragupta Maurya is counted among the great rulers of India. He was the first emperor of the Mauryan Empire. He was the first emperor who established his rule over a vast territory, and the extent of his empire was larger than the British Indian Empire. The boundary of his empire touched Iran. He was the first to politically unify India.

stem: Who was the founder of the Maurya Empire?
expl: The Maurya dynasty was founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Its period was 321–184 BCE. After this, the Kushana dynasty, the Gupta dynasty, and the Vardhana dynasty ruled ancient India.

stem: Who amongst the following Mauryan rulers did conquered the Deccan?
expl: Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Mauryan Empire, conquered South India (the Deccan). In this regard, information is obtained from Ashoka’s inscriptions, and from Jain and Tamil sources. Ashoka’s inscriptions are found at many places in the southern region, but Ashoka carried out only the Kalinga conquest. Therefore, the credit for conquest in the south has to be given to Chandragupta Maurya, because Bindusara’s conquests are highly doubtful and he is not remembered in history as a conqueror. Jain and Tamil sources also confirm Chandragupta Maurya’s southern conquest.

stem: Chandragupta Maurya figures prominently in the book of –
expl: Detailed information about Chandragupta Maurya is obtained from Vishakhadatta’s 'Mudrarakshasa'. In this work, Chandragupta is considered the son of Mahapadma Nanda (another name—Nanda). In Mudrarakshasa, Chandragupta is also called “Vrishala” and “Kulheen.” In the 18th century CE, Dhundhiraj wrote a commentary on Mudrarakshasa.

stem: Megasthenes was the ambassador of -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/ More than one of the above

expl: Megasthenes was a Greek ambassador sent by Seleucus Nicator to the royal court of Chandragupta Maurya. Earlier, he had served as Seleucus’s envoy in the royal court of the satrap of Arachosia.

stem: In how many categories did Megasthenes divide the Indian society?
expl: In his book Indica, Megasthenes divided Indian society into seven categories—(1) Philosophers, (2) Farmers, (3) Herders, (4) Craftsmen and businessmen, (5) Warriors, (6) Inspectors, and (7) Ministers and preachers. Megasthenes does not mention the prevalence of slavery in Indian society. In the Mauryan period, no person could marry outside his caste, nor could he adopt an occupation different from it.

stem: The description of the administration of Pataliputra is available in?
expl: The administration of the city of Pataliputra is found in Megasthenes’ Indica. Megasthenes mentions six committees, each consisting of five members, of the municipal council of Pataliputra. He calls the city officials Astynomoi.

stem: The inscription which proves Chandragupta’s sway over western India is:
expl: From the Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman I (150 CE), it is known that Pushyagupta, the provincial governor of Chandragupta Maurya in Saurashtra, had Sudarshana Lake constructed there, and later Tushaspa, described as a Yavana ruler in Ashoka’s time, built canals connected with this reservoir. This province has been referred to as Anarta and Surashtra. This provides evidence of Chandragupta Maurya’s overlordship over western India.

stem: In which inscription is Kalinga victory is mentioned?

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: The mention of Ashoka’s Kalinga conquest is found in Ashoka’s 13th Major Rock Edict. The Hathigumpha inscription is an autobiographical account of the Chedi king Kharavela. This cave is located on the Udayagiri hill near Bhubaneswar.

stem: Which one territory of the following was not a part of Ashoka’s empire?
expl: Sri Lanka was not included in Ashoka’s empire. Ashoka’s Second Rock Edict indicates that Ashoka’s authority in India extended everywhere except Chola, Pandya, Satiyaputta, Keralaputta, and Tamraparni (Sri Lanka). These states were called Pratyanta, i.e., frontier/border states.

stem: The only pillar on which Ashoka declares himself as the emperor of Magadha –
expl: In the Bhabru (Bairat) rock inscription, Ashoka described himself as the Emperor of Magadha—(Priyadasi laja Magadhe sanghe abhivadetoonam aaha apaba dhatam cha …). This inscription also establishes Ashoka as a follower of Buddhism.

stem: The central point in Ashoka's Dhamma is -

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: Ashoka’s Dhamma (Dharma) was a moral code. Through his second and seventh pillar edicts, Ashoka conveys the message—“Apasinave bahukayane daya dane, sache sochaye madave sadhave cha.” That is, do less wrongdoing, do welfare, show compassion and charity, speak the truth, live with purity, maintain gentleness in nature, and uphold goodness. Thus, the basic message of Ashoka’s Dhamma includes peace and non-violence, respect for elders, and religious tolerance. Therefore, the correct answer is option (e).

stem: The name by which Ashoka is referred to in his inscriptions is :

options.label: e
options.text: None of the above/More than one of the above

expl: In most of Ashoka’s inscriptions, he is addressed with titles such as Devanampiya, Devanampiya Piyadashi (Beloved of the Gods / pleasant to look at), and Raja, etc. In the Puranas, he is called Ashokvardhana.

stem: Language used in the inscriptions of Ashoka is:
expl: Ashoka’s history is known mainly from his inscriptions. His inscriptions can be classified into three categories—(1) Rock Edicts, (2) Pillar Edicts, and (3) Cave Inscriptions. The Rock Edicts are a group of 14 different edicts, found at eight different places—(1) Shahbazgarhi, (2) Mansehra, (3) Kalsi, (4) Girnar, (5) Dhauli, (6) Jaugada, (7) Erragudi, and (8) Sopara. Most of Ashoka’s inscriptions are written in the Prakrit language and Brahmi script; only two—Shahbazgarhi and Mansehra—are in Kharosthi script (not Brahmi). A broken inscription written in Aramaic was found from Taxila; a bilingual inscription (Greek and Syriac) was found from a place called Sherekhuna; and an Ashokan inscription written in Aramaic was also found from Laghman.

stem: Which one of the following scripts was written from right to left in ancient India?
expl: In ancient India, the Kharoshthi script was written from right to left. The credit for reading it is given to scholars such as Prinsep (1835 A.D.), Grotefend (1836 A.D.), Lassen (1838 A.D.), etc. It was mainly a script of north-western India.

stem: Which ruler had made Pataliputra the capital of his empire for the first time?
expl: In fact, Pataliputra was founded by Udayin, a ruler of the Haryanka dynasty, at the confluence of the Ganga and Son rivers, and he shifted his capital from Rajagriha to Pataliputra. However, since Udayin is not given in the options, Chandragupta Maurya is the correct answer.

stem: Who was the last ruler of the Mauryan dynasty?
expl: The last Mauryan ruler was Brihadratha. He was killed by his commander Pushyamitra Shunga in 184 B.C. The founder of the Maurya dynasty was Chandragupta Maurya. Chandragupta Maurya is counted among the great rulers of India. He was an emperor who established his rule over a vast region of India.

stem: The most famous centre of learning during the Mauryan period was:
expl: Vaishali is currently a district of Bihar. In ancient times, Vaishali was associated with Buddhism and Jainism. In the 6th century B.C., it was a major republican state under the Vajji confederacy. Mahavira was born at Kundagram in Vaishali. Nalanda was an important centre of Buddhist education. The first Buddhist monastery here was established in the Gupta period. Taxila was a major centre of Hindu and Buddhist education in the Mauryan period. Students came here to study from across the world.
